questions.question: What does a Flat index provide that approximate indexes do not?
options: Exact nearest-neighbor results for the selected metric
questions.explanation: Flat search examines the full corpus and is the ground-truth baseline for recall evaluation.

questions.question: What does nprobe control for an IVF index?
options: How many inverted cells are searched
questions.explanation: Searching more cells usually improves recall while increasing distance work and latency.

questions.question: Why use Product Quantization?
options: To store compact lossy codes and reduce memory
questions.explanation: PQ trades representation detail for much smaller per-vector storage.

questions.question: What must be versioned with a serialized FAISS index?
options: Embedding model, dimensions, metric, normalization, IDs, metadata, parameters, and evaluation evidence
questions.explanation: Search correctness depends on the complete vector-space and result-hydration contract.

questions.question: How should approximate recall be measured?
options: Compare results with exact Flat ground truth on representative queries
Infer it from index size alone
questions.explanation: Recall@K requires known nearest neighbors from an exact baseline and a representative query distribution.

questions.question: Why publish an index generation atomically?
options: To prevent queries from observing mismatched index and metadata versions
questions.explanation: The serving pointer should expose one coherent generation at a time.
